title: Edit Video by Chatting
subtitle: You type what you want, AI cuts the video for you
intro: Your saves say RIP to DaVinci, iMovie and CapCut. You can now edit just by chatting with AI.
takeaway: Prompt-based editing trades timeline control for speed, so check what the AI guessed wrong.

sections.heading: Analogy: talking to an editor
sections.body:
Think of AI editing like texting a human editor instead of moving clips yourself.

You say "remove silences, add captions, make me an avatar" and it does it. One prompt replaces dozens of clicks.

That sounds like magic, but why did we need it?

sections.heading: Why it exists: speed you don't pay for twice
sections.body:
A prompt is an instruction in plain words. Transcript-based editing turns your speech into text you can delete to cut video.

Your saves show HeyGen cloning a creator to 50M+ views from just text, image or audio. Veo 3 even lets you use JSON prompts for precise control of lighting and cuts.

Fast is great until the AI misunderstands you.

sections.heading: What can go wrong: when chatting breaks
sections.body:
AI guesses what you meant. Vague prompts give wrong cuts, weird avatar mouths, or off-brand styles.

JSON helps, but more detail means more to fix if you typo. You still need to review every auto-cut.

So start simple, then add control only where it matters.

options: It gives precise control over lighting, style and cuts

quiz.q: What breaks first if you rely only on vague prompts for 100 videos?
options: AI makes wrong cuts and inconsistent style you must re-edit
Your computer runs out of battery
quiz.why: Vague prompts cause AI to guess, leading to errors in cuts, avatars and style at scale.
